reason: Both catch the same core defects (survivorship bias, self-selection confound, multiple comparisons, region causation gap, satisfaction causation gap, points-vs-percent), but Response B additionally separates out two valid, distinct defects that A only buries in a consequence clause: that mandating webinars extrapolates the voluntary-attendance effect to a different (compelled) population, and that the retention figure lacks any significance/sample-size reporting unlike the region claim — making B's analysis marginally more complete and precise.
